title: Stress-driven HPA dysregulation — normal fueling, autonomic load
description: User's cycles disrupted but no LEA signature — activity, sleep duration, weight all stable; stress-high seconds are very elevated (28,400/day vs typical 8-12k for a calmer baseline), follicular HRV is unusually low at 38, sleep latency runs >25 min. This is the stress-driven sub-phenotype of FHA described in KB2 rather than the under-fueling sub-phenotype. Stress-tests ET11 (CBT referral per KB2 first-line for psychological dimension), and inverse-CF1 (low HRV in someone fueling normally → autonomic load, not LEA).

user_reported_context: Last period was Dec 8, 2025 — nothing since. Started a high-stress new role around the same time (consulting, frequent travel, intermittent sleep). Eating normally, weight stable, exercising moderately. No history of restriction or HA before this. Recently broke up with long-term partner.
notes: Tests whether v3.x correctly identifies the stress-driven sub-phenotype rather than defaulting to LEA framing. Key indicators that this is NOT classic LEA: normal RHR (not bradycardic), HRV is LOW not high (sympathetic dominance, not parasympathetic), no energy-deficit markers in activity or weight. CBT is first-line per KB2 ('we recommend cognitive behavior therapy after ruling out organic causes'). Actionable test should be autonomic-downregulation-focused (NSDR, breathwork, wind-down protocol) with stress-high-seconds as the measurable signal. Escalation should refer to a CBT-trained therapist with HA/ED familiarity per ET11.
